target.title: fix(cli): one-shot agent --local runs never export OTel diagnostics
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Fixes an issue where one-shot `openclaw agent --local` runs would export no OTel telemetry at all when `diagnostics.otel.enabled: true` and the `diagnostics-otel` plugin are configured: zero spans, metrics, or logs reached the OTLP collector, while the same turns dispatched through the Gateway exported fine. Gateway-to-embedded fallback runs (gateway timeout or transport failure) silently dropped telemetry the same way, so exactly the runs that bypass the Gateway were invisible in tracing backends.

## Why This Change Was Made

Diagnostics exporters are plugin services and were only ever started inside the Gateway process (`startPluginServices` at gateway startup/reload); embedded CLI runs emit diagnostic events in the CLI process where nothing subscribes. The CLI now starts the `diagnostics-otel` service around embedded agent runs via a scoped, non-activating plugin load that honors the same plugin-enablement config as the Gateway, and flushes on exit: drain the async diagnostic-event queue, then shut the SDK down (force flush), bounded by a 10s timeout so an unreachable collector cannot hang the CLI. `diagnostics-prometheus` intentionally stays Gateway-only — it is a pull-based scrape server that is useless in a short-lived process and would race the Gateway for its port. No new config surface; configs without OTel enabled short-circuit before any plugin load.

## User Impact

Operators running one-shot `openclaw agent --local` turns (and runs that fall back from the Gateway to the embedded agent) now get the same OTel traces, metrics, and logs as Gateway-executed turns, flushed before the process exits. Setups without OTel export enabled are unaffected.

## Evidence

- Live before/after on macOS against a local Arize Phoenix OTLP collector: before, one-shot `--local` runs produced zero spans while Gateway runs exported fine; after, a one-shot run logs `diagnostics-otel: logs exporter enabled (OTLP/Protobuf)` and `openclaw.harness.run`, `openclaw.run`, and `openclaw.model.call` spans (with `gen_ai.*` attributes) arrive in Phoenix seconds after the process exits.
- New focused tests: `src/plugins/one-shot-diagnostics.test.ts` covers config gating (no plugin load when OTel is off), the scoped non-activating load, exporter allowlist filtering, drain-before-stop ordering, and the flush timeout bound; `src/commands/agent-via-gateway.test.ts` adds cases for start/flush ordering around local runs, flush when the embedded run fails, run survival when exporter startup fails, exporter start on gateway-to-embedded fallback, and no exporter on Gateway dispatch. Both files pass (9 + 73 tests) rebased on current `main`.
- `pnpm build` clean with no `[INEFFECTIVE_DYNAMIC_IMPORT]` warnings; `tsgo` core and test lanes clean; oxfmt/oxlint clean on touched files. Validation ran locally via `scripts/run-vitest.mjs` (remote Testbox was unavailable in this environment).

## What Problem This Solves

Memory recall can currently receive the conversation/session context without a stable indication of which group participant authored the triggering message. In multi-person channels, that can make retrieved or promoted memory read as if another participant's facts belong to the operator. ## Summary

- Carries `SourceActor` from inbound context through embedded runs and plugin tool context.
- Exposes the same source actor context to memory corpus supplements for `memory_search` and `memory_get`.
- Reuses the typed `SourceActorRole` contract across reply runtime, plugin tool context, and memory context.
- Adds memory prompt/flush guidance to preserve participant attribution instead of merging another participant's facts into the operator/user profile.

## Scope and honesty

This PR carries `SourceActor` context into memory recall and adds prompt/flush guidance to preserve participant attribution. It is the plumbing + guidance layer: it makes attribution available and instructs the model to keep it. It does NOT yet structurally enforce attribution on stored memories (e.g., tagging persisted entries with the source actor) -- that is a follow-up. Best-effort: recall tracking never blocks recall.

target.title: fix(signal): detect native bot mentions in group gating
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Signal groups can be configured with `requireMention=true` so side chatter stays quiet until the bot is explicitly mentioned. Signal native mentions arrive as structured `dataMessage.mentions[]` metadata plus object-replacement characters in the message text. The current Signal handler renders those placeholders as `@<uuid>` or `@<phone>`, then relies on text mention regexes. Selecting the bot from Signal's native mention UI can therefore fail to wake the bot unless a matching text fallback happens to be configured.

This also leaves `canDetectMention` tied only to configured text regexes and passes `hasAnyMention=false` even when Signal supplied structured mention metadata.

## Why This Change Was Made

This patch keeps the fix inside the Signal plugin and adds a small native mention fact resolver. It compares structured Signal mention metadata against the current bot account identity:

- UUID via `channels.signal.accountUuid`
- phone number via the existing E.164 normalizer and `channels.signal.account`

The event handler now combines text fallback and native metadata:

- `wasMentioned` is true for text fallback or a native mention that targets the current bot account.
- `canDetectMention` reflects text regexes or available bot account identity.
- `hasAnyMention` reflects valid structured Signal mention metadata so the shared mention-decision contract can distinguish command bypass from messages mentioning someone else.

Mentions of other participants do not trigger the bot. Missing bot identity does not become a false mention. Existing text fallback, group access checks, pending history, attachment restraint, control-command handling, direct messages, and `requireMention=false` behavior stay unchanged.

This supersedes #69413, which was closed without merge, by adding the missing capability facts, event-handler coverage, and docs.

## User Impact

Before:

> A user could select the bot from Signal's native mention UI in a `requireMention` group and get no response because the rendered `@uuid`/`@phone` text did not match the configured agent-name regex.

After:

> Native Signal mentions targeting the current bot account pass mention gating. Mentions of other participants remain silent and are kept only as bounded pending context. A later bot mention can include recent skipped group context and reply in the same group.

Docs now describe Signal native mention behavior, `accountUuid`, text mention fallback, and a mention-gated group configuration with bounded history.

### Behavior Change

Signal groups with `requireMention=true` that have a configured bot identity (`accountUuid`/`account`) but no text mention regexes previously fell through to pass-through handling. After this change they enforce mention gating via native Signal mention metadata. Group chatter that did not mention the bot but previously reached it may now be gated. This is intended and makes native-only `requireMention` groups behave as documented. Maintainers with such groups should expect stricter, correct gating after upgrade.

### Trust Model

`dataMessage.mentions[]` is sender-supplied. A group member could craft metadata naming the bot; the only effect is waking the bot, which any member can already do via a normal Signal mention. Native facts are still validated against a real object-replacement placeholder span, so malformed metadata does not become a bot mention.

### Native Identity Note

For full native mention coverage, configure `channels.signal.accountUuid` alongside `channels.signal.account`. Phone-only identity can still match phone-backed mention metadata, but UUID-only Signal mention metadata requires `accountUuid`.

## Evidence

- Base: `4ecb45b chore: update default check gate expectations`
- Head: `83ac15c979a4`
- Static whitespace check: `git diff --check HEAD~1..HEAD`
- Focused Signal mention-gating tests passed on this branch:
  `node scripts/run-vitest.mjs extensions/signal/src/monitor/event-handler.mention-gating.test.ts`
- Production TypeScript check passed:
  `pnpm tsgo:prod`

The focused Signal suite covers:

- native bot UUID mention without text mention patterns;
- native bot phone mention with E.164 normalization;
- native mention of another participant stays silent and records pending context;
- malformed matching metadata does not become a bot mention;
- no-detector behavior remains explicit;
- helper facts for bot mention, unrelated mention, malformed span, and missing bot identity.

### Redacted Live Signal Proof

This is the sanitized inspectable artifact from a live 3-person private Signal smoke. IDs, UUIDs, phone numbers, group IDs, raw message bodies, and private participant context are intentionally omitted.

```text

runtime: OpenClaw gateway with this PR's Signal mention patch installed
config.runtime: { signalConfigured: true, groupPolicy: "allowlist", groupAllowFromCount: 1, groupsCount: 1, requireMentionGroups: 1, accountUuidSet: true, historyLimit: 3 }
config.template: { signalConfigured: true, groupPolicy: "allowlist", groupAllowFromCount: 1, groupsCount: 1, requireMentionGroups: 1, accountUuidSet: true, historyLimit: 3 }

observed: no bot reply was produced after the quiet window
```

target.title: fix(mobile): clarify gateway connection security setup
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Manual gateway setup on Android and iOS used ambiguous `Local` and `TLS` controls. Users could enter a remote hostname while the app still targeted loopback, select transport security without understanding the effective endpoint, or receive protocol/TLS failures without a concrete recovery step.

## Why This Change Was Made

Both mobile apps now:

- present connection security as `Unencrypted` or `Secure (TLS)`
- require secure transport for non-private hosts
- preview the effective `ws://` or `wss://` endpoint without replacing user-facing labels with protocol syntax
- provide actionable TLS guidance
- provide a copyable `openclaw update` command for gateway protocol mismatch

Remote-host security selection is deterministic local policy based on the entered host. It does not ping, probe, or otherwise preflight the gateway.

This PR is AI-assisted.

## User Impact

Android and iOS users get the same connection model and recovery guidance during onboarding and later manual gateway configuration. Remote connections can no longer silently retain a loopback-oriented mode, and error states explain the operator action needed to recover.

## Evidence

- Android focused unit tests and debug build passed.
- iOS focused tests passed: 23 tests, 0 failures.
- Fresh pre-commit `$autoreview` completed with no actionable findings.
- `git diff --check` passes on the rebased branch.
- Before/after screenshots are attached in the [mobile UI evidence comment](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/101325#issuecomment-4899867668); no image assets are committed to the repository.

target.title: [AI-assisted] Add session history family lookup
target.body:
## Problem

When a threaded conversation has already been split across reset transcripts, `chat.history` and the `sessions_history` tool only read the currently active transcript. The session store can already retain the family through `usageFamilySessionIds`, but history readers do not use that chain and do not discover archived `*.jsonl.reset.<timestamp>` topic transcripts.

That means an agent/tool can be looking at the correct logical Telegram/Slack/Discord thread and still miss earlier turns after session rollover.

## Fix

Add an opt-in family history path:

- `chat.history` accepts `includeFamily: true`.
- `sessions_history` accepts `includeFamily`.
- Gateway and embedded `chat.history` now share the bounded/header-checked reset archive resolver instead of using separate prefix scans.
- The shared resolver can include owned topic-suffixed reset archives such as `<sessionId>-topic-456.jsonl.reset.<timestamp>` only when the archive header matches the requested session id.
- Same-prefix colliding topic archives and headerless topic archives are ignored.
- Family read targets are capped before transcript reads, and normal `chat.history` behavior remains opt-in: UI startup does not load ancestor history.

## Validation

Current head: `1aa4e9cbb94f6841803bd55559aa0ea6de17dc67`.

- `CI=true node scripts/run-vitest.mjs run src/gateway/server.chat.gateway-server-chat-b.test.ts src/agents/tools/embedded-gateway-stub.test.ts`
  - gateway shard: 84 tests passed
  - agents shard: 11 tests passed
- `CI=true node scripts/run-vitest.mjs run src/agents/openclaw-tools.sessions.test.ts`
  - 36 tests passed
- `CI=true node --import tsx scripts/generate-prompt-snapshots.ts --check`
  - `Prompt snapshots are current (7 files).`
- `CI=true node scripts/run-tsgo.mjs -p test/tsconfig/tsconfig.core.test.json --incremental --tsBuildInfoFile .artifacts/tsgo-cache/core-test.tsbuildinfo`
  - passed
- `CI=true node scripts/run-tsgo.mjs -p test/tsconfig/tsconfig.extensions.test.json --incremental --tsBuildInfoFile .artifacts/tsgo-cache/extensions-test.tsbuildinfo`
  - passed
- `git diff --check`
  - passed, no output

## Real Behavior Proof

- **Behavior or issue addressed:** A logical thread whose active session has `usageFamilySessionIds` should be able to fetch earlier reset transcript turns when a caller explicitly requests family history, including owned topic-suffixed reset archives, without reading colliding or headerless topic archives. The current active transcript must also be preserved when a retained reset family has more entries than the bounded 32 read targets.
- **Real environment tested:** Local OpenClaw checkout on this PR branch at current head `a12e1bbcf0`, using temporary on-disk session directories, the real Gateway `chat.history` RPC integration harness, embedded-mode `chat.history`, and the same reset archive filename/header patterns that OpenClaw creates for topic transcripts.
- **Exact steps or command run after this patch:**
  1. Created temporary session directories and session-store entries with `usageFamilySessionIds` linking an ancestor session and the current session.
  2. Wrote an owned plain ancestor reset archive and an owned topic-suffixed ancestor archive with matching `type: "session"` headers.
  3. Wrote newer same-prefix colliding and headerless topic reset archives in the same sessions directory.
  4. Invoked the real Gateway `chat.history` RPC path with and without `includeFamily: true`.
  5. Created a second Gateway/RPC case with 40 ancestor session ids before the current id in `usageFamilySessionIds`.
  6. Invoked embedded-mode `chat.history(includeFamily)` through the sessions tool stub, including the same >32-family-target cap case.
- **Evidence after fix:** Terminal capture from current head:
  ```text
  $ CI=true node scripts/run-vitest.mjs run src/gateway/server.chat.gateway-server-chat-b.test.ts src/agents/tools/embedded-gateway-stub.test.ts
  Test Files  2 passed (2)

  [test] passed 2 Vitest shards in 44.69s

  Test Files  1 passed (1)
  Tests  36 passed (36)
  [test] passed 1 Vitest shard in 30.16s

  Prompt snapshots are current (7 files).

  # passed
  ```

- **Observed result after fix:** Default `chat.history` excludes ancestor reset archive content, while `chat.history(includeFamily)` includes the owned plain ancestor archive, includes the owned topic-suffixed ancestor archive, includes current-session content, and rejects the colliding/headerless topic reset archives. In the >32-target Gateway/RPC regression, `chat.history(includeFamily)` contains `current survives family target cap`, contains early ancestor content, and does not read the ancestor entries beyond the target cap. Embedded `chat.history(includeFamily)` now reads the current active transcript first, then current archives, then ancestor archives/active transcripts; its >32-target regression also keeps the current transcript and drops over-cap ancestors.
- **What was not tested:** I did not run a live Telegram topic end-to-end, and this PR does not add prompt-level carryover summaries or automatic prompt injection. It only adds explicit family history retrieval for gateway/tool callers.

target.title: fix(web): avoid exact-limit fetch truncation warnings
target.body:
﻿Closes #101837

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes an issue where users running `web_fetch` could see a response reported as truncated when the streamed response body was exactly `maxResponseBytes` bytes, even though no bytes were omitted.

## Why This Change Was Made

`readResponseText` now treats truncation as proven only when a chunk exceeds the remaining byte budget. Reaching the byte budget exactly no longer flips the truncation flag by itself, so exact-limit responses can complete normally while true overflow still cancels the reader.

## User Impact

Users no longer get misleading `Response body truncated after ... bytes.` warnings for complete responses that happen to land exactly on the byte cap. Oversized responses are still bounded and marked truncated.

## Evidence

- Claim proved: Current head `18b610b93e7e0a96de0eb891de3bab0e43f2c74b` lets an exact-limit `readResponseText` helper run complete without setting `truncated`, while still reporting the exact byte count.
- Real helper proof for the requested boundary, constructing a real `Response` from streamed chunks `"hello"` + `" world"` and reading it with `maxBytes: 11`:
  ```text
  node --import ../openclaw/node_modules/tsx/dist/esm/index.mjs --input-type=module -e "import { readResponseText } from './src/agents/tools/web-shared.ts'; const encoder = new TextEncoder(); let cancelCount = 0; const response = new Response(new ReadableStream({ start(controller) { controller.enqueue(encoder.encode('hello')); controller.enqueue(encoder.encode(' world')); controller.close(); }, cancel() { cancelCount += 1; } })); const result = await readResponseText(response, { maxBytes: 11 }); console.log(JSON.stringify({ text: result.text, truncated: result.truncated, bytesRead: result.bytesRead, cancelCount }));"
  {"text":"hello world","truncated":false,"bytesRead":11,"cancelCount":0}
  ```
- Focused regression: `PNPM_CONFIG_MODULES_DIR='../openclaw/node_modules' node scripts/run-vitest.mjs src/agents/tools/web-shared.test.ts` passed (`1` file, `12` tests).
- Whitespace check: `git diff --check` passed.

Observed result: exact-limit helper output is `truncated:false`, `bytesRead:11`, and `cancelCount:0`, so the shared helper no longer feeds a false truncation warning to `web_fetch` for complete exact-cap responses.

target.body:
> [!NOTE]
> **AI-Assisted Contribution:** This PR was prepared and validated with the assistance of an AI coding assistant (Antigravity/Gemini).

## What Problem This Solves
Resolves a problem where the model auth subsystem ignores explicit `apiKey` (literal or SecretRef) overrides in `models.json` if store profiles exist (pr #100839).

**Symptom/Behavior:**
1. Unless `auth: "api-key"` is explicitly set (making `shouldPreferExplicitConfigApiKeyAuth` true), the literal key or SecretRef configured in `models.json` is ignored during the binding phase (falling through `providerEntryBinding` checks). The function then scans the profile store; if any profile is found for the provider, it overrides the user's explicit `apiKey` configuration.
2. Additionally, when a specific profile was requested (e.g. during failover rotation or pinned session), the early check for explicit models.json `apiKey` would bypass profile resolution entirely and return the models.json `apiKey` instead of the rotated profile, causing E2E failover tests (`rotates for overloaded assistant failures across auto-pinned profiles`) to fail.
3. In `models status` and `models auth list` commands, placeholder/marker values in the environment (e.g. `GOOGLE_API_KEY`) were treated as literal keys, causing incorrect `effective=models.json` formatting instead of falling back to store profiles.

Affected locations:
- [resolveApiKeyForProvider](file:///home/dietpi/Developer/openclaw/src/agents/model-auth.ts#L1071-L1084)
- [resolveProviderAuthOverview](file:///home/dietpi/Developer/openclaw/src/commands/models/list.auth-overview.ts#L152-L163)

## Why This Change Was Made
Implemented a surgical fix to resolve the logic discrepancy and test failures:

target.title: add per-conversation whatsapp debounce config
target.body:
## Summary

Adds per-conversation inbound debounce configuration for WhatsApp direct chats and groups.

Practically, this controls how long OpenClaw waits before starting an agent turn after receiving a WhatsApp message from a specific conversation. This is useful when a contact sends multiple messages in a row: OpenClaw can wait a few seconds or minutes, collect the full burst, and then let the agent process the conversation with better context.

## What Problem This Solves

The existing WhatsApp debounce setting is too broad for mixed usage.

Some conversations should be processed immediately, while others should wait briefly:

- owner/admin chats often need immediate processing, so they can use `debounceMs: 0`
- external contacts often send multiple short messages in a row, so they can use a longer debounce, such as `180000`, to wait 3 minutes
- noisy groups can have their own debounce window
- wildcard entries can define defaults for all direct chats or all groups

This lets operators tune batching by conversation without changing the global WhatsApp debounce for every chat.

## Behavior

- supports `debounceMs` in `channels.whatsapp.direct`
- supports `debounceMs` in `channels.whatsapp.groups`
- supports wildcard entries like `direct["*"]` and `groups["*"]`
- specific conversation config wins over wildcard config
- falls back to the existing global WhatsApp debounce when no conversation override exists
- `debounceMs: 0` disables debounce for that conversation only

Closes #52972

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes an issue where users who schedule reminders through a shell-driven `openclaw cron add ...` command could still receive the false note saying no reminder was scheduled in the turn.

## Why This Change Was Made

The reminder guard already trusts successful structured `cron` tool adds. This extends the same producer-side counter to successful `exec` and `bash` commands that run `openclaw cron add` and return a cron add response shaped like the CLI output.

The repair also handles the CLI warning path where `openclaw cron add --message ...` emits the missing-agent warning on stderr while still printing the successful JSON receipt on stdout. Exec aggregates stdout and stderr, so the parser now scans the aggregate for a valid cron-add JSON receipt instead of requiring the whole aggregate to be pure JSON. Failed commands and unrelated cron commands are ignored.

## User Impact

Users no longer get a contradictory unscheduled-reminder note after a shell cron add succeeds, including the default-agent warning case. Failed or unrelated shell commands still leave the guard active.

## Evidence

## What Problem This Solves

`loadBootFile` in `src/gateway/boot.ts` read the workspace `BOOT.md` with an unbounded `fs.readFile`, allowing an arbitrarily large file to be loaded into memory during gateway boot.

## Why This Change Was Made

Switch to `readRegularFile` from `../infra/regular-file.js` with a 16 MiB cap, matching the pattern used for other bounded file reads. The helper also rejects symlinks and non-file targets. An oversized `BOOT.md` is treated as empty/missing so the boot step is skipped safely instead of failing or allocating excessive memory.

## User Impact

No behavioral change for normal `BOOT.md` files. Pathologically large `BOOT.md` files are now handled safely and consistently: the boot check is skipped rather than attempting an unbounded read.

## Evidence

- Added regression test in `src/gateway/boot.test.ts` that creates a `16 MiB + 1` byte `BOOT.md` and asserts `runBootOnce` returns `{ status: "skipped", reason: "empty" }`.
- Local focused run: `node scripts/run-vitest.mjs src/gateway/boot.test.ts --run` passes (68/68 tests across gateway configs).

## Summary

Stacked after #101328. This adds the first read-only Claw feed layer so OpenClaw can discover a Claw from a feed entry and build the same lifecycle plan introduced in PR2.

Design reference: RFC PR https://github.com/openclaw/rfcs/pull/27

- adds `openclaw.clawFeed.v1` types, strict parsing, and local feed file reading
- resolves feed entries to local Claw manifest sources with source-locality checks
- adds owner/trust metadata on feed entries and warnings for missing owner evidence
- adds `openclaw claws feed inspect <feed>` and `openclaw claws feed plan <feed> <claw>`
- keeps PR3 read-only: remote feed fetch, install, mutation, and ClawHub publish/search stay deferred

## Safety / ownership behavior

- relative feed sources must stay under the feed file directory
- absolute local paths are rejected
- remote `http`/`https` sources are rejected in this PR
- `file:` URLs are accepted only if they resolve under the feed directory
- feed entry id must match the resolved manifest id
- feed entry version mismatch is diagnostic-only warning so feeds can surface drift without mutating anything

target.title: fix(discord): split encoded video URLs from captions
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Fixes a Discord outbound send edge case where a caption + video URL can miss the existing caption-first/media-second split when the URL encodes the extension dot, such as `render%2Emp4`.

The split decision depends on Discord's local video URL classification. `new URL(...).pathname` preserves `%2E`, so a path like `/attachments/1/render%2Emp4` did not match the existing `.mp4` / `.webm` / `.mov` suffix check and was treated as non-video.

## Why This Change Was Made

The production change is intentionally small and stays inside Discord's local media detector:

```diff
 const parsed = new URL(trimmed);
-return normalizeLowercaseStringOrEmpty(parsed.pathname);
+try {
+  return normalizeLowercaseStringOrEmpty(decodeURIComponent(parsed.pathname));
+} catch {
+  return normalizeLowercaseStringOrEmpty(parsed.pathname);
+}
```

This decodes URL pathnames before video-extension matching, while preserving the previous fallback for malformed percent encoding. Local non-URL paths still use the existing query/hash stripping path, and the original `mediaUrl` is still passed through to the Discord send call.

## User Impact

Discord outbound sends with a caption and an encoded video extension now follow the same behavior covered by the existing video split path: the caption text is sent first, then the video media is sent separately.

For example, `https://cdn.discordapp.com/attachments/1/render%2Emp4?ex=1` now classifies like a normal `.mp4` URL for the Discord caption/video split decision.

## Evidence

Local validation:

- `git diff --check` passed.
- `node scripts/run-vitest.mjs run extensions/discord/src/outbound-adapter.test.ts` passed with 1 test file and 48 tests.

Production-path terminal proof:

This proof imports the real Discord outbound adapter and calls `discordOutbound.sendMedia` with the encoded-dot video URL. The only injected part is the final Discord send transport, so the transcript can observe whether the production outbound adapter chooses one combined send or the caption-first/media-second split.

```text
[proof] Discord outbound production adapter with injected Discord send transport
[proof] input mediaUrl=https://cdn.discordapp.com/attachments/1/render%2Emp4?ex=1
[proof] send call count=2
[proof] call 1: {"target":"channel:redacted-discord-channel","content":"rendered clip","mediaUrl":null,"reply":{"messageId":"reply-1","scope":"all"},"accountId":"default"}
[proof] call 2: {"target":"channel:redacted-discord-channel","content":"","mediaUrl":"https://cdn.discordapp.com/attachments/1/render%2Emp4?ex=1","reply":{"messageId":"reply-1","scope":"all"},"accountId":"default"}
[proof] returned={"channel":"discord","messageId":"proof-2","channelId":"redacted-discord-channel"}
[proof] PASS: encoded-dot video URL takes caption-first/media-second outbound path
```

Focused behavior covered by the regression test:

```text
mediaUrl = https://cdn.discordapp.com/attachments/1/render%2Emp4?ex=1
caption send -> sendMessageDiscord(..., "rendered clip", ...)
media send   -> sendMessageDiscord(..., "", { mediaUrl })
```

Call chain / impact:

```text
discordOutbound captioned media send
-> normalizeMediaPathForExtension(mediaUrl)
-> URL pathname extraction
-> video extension check
-> caption/media split decision
```

Scope and sibling surfaces:

- Production diff is limited to `extensions/discord/src/media-detection.ts` and changes only URL pathname normalization before suffix detection.
- The test change extends the existing Discord outbound split test in `extensions/discord/src/outbound-adapter.test.ts` instead of adding a new broad test surface.
- No shared media-core helper is changed; this PR intentionally scopes the fix to Discord's local caption/video split detector.
- Malformed percent encoding still falls back to the original URL pathname, so this does not add a new send-time exception path.

Live-proof note:

- This local environment does not expose Discord live smoke credentials (`DISCORD_*` / `OPENCLAW_*DISCORD*` env vars were absent), and the repository's Discord live QA workflow requires maintainer-level repository access. The terminal proof above exercises the production outbound decision path and redacts the channel id.

But several agent-facing descriptors and public docs still said `memory/*.md`, which can mislead agents into thinking the index is flat.
- This PR updates the remaining stale references to `memory/**/*.md`. No runtime behavior change.

## Files touched
- `extensions/memory-core/index.ts` — lazy `memory_search` / `memory_get` descriptors
- `extensions/memory-core/src/tools.ts` — concrete `memory_search` / `memory_get` descriptions
- `extensions/memory-core/src/prompt-section.ts` — system-prompt recall guidance

## Note
This supersedes #72748. That PR also carried QMD watcher changes that were independently resolved upstream by #81802 (`watch-settle.ts`), so the surviving value was just this wording alignment. Splitting it out as a small, behavior-neutral PR for easier review.

## Real behavior proof

**Behavior or issue addressed**: Agent-facing descriptors and public docs said `memory/*.md` even though the runtime already walks `memory/` recursively and indexes nested files such as `memory/YYYY-MM/YYYY-MM-DD.md`. This PR aligns the wording to `memory/**/*.md` so agents and readers see what is actually indexed. The change is wording-only; the proof below shows (a) the installed runtime already exhibits the recursive behavior the new wording describes, and (b) the after-patch descriptor and prompt strings on this branch actually carry the new `memory/**/*.md` wording when imported at runtime.

target.body:
## Summary

- Problem: Barnacle auto-response doesn't resync candidate labels when a draft PR is marked `ready_for_review`, leaving stale candidate labels (e.g. `triage: blank-template`) on PRs with meaningful bodies.
- Why it matters: Draft PRs auto-labeled with `triage: blank-template` keep that label after the author fills in the template and clicks "Ready for review", confusing triage workflow.
- What changed: Added `ready_for_review` to the auto-response workflow trigger and script allowlist; rewrote `applyPullRequestCandidateLabels` to compute and remove stale candidate labels while preserving suppression/privileged-author guards.
- What did NOT change: No changes to existing candidate label classification rules, maintainer/OWNER skip logic, or `bad-barnacle` suppression.

## Change Type (select all)

- [x] Bug fix
- [x] CI/CD / infra

## Scope (select all touched areas)

- [x] CI/CD / infra

## Linked Issue/PR

- Closes #77343
- [x] This PR fixes a bug or regression

## Root Cause (if applicable)

- Root cause: Three gaps — (1) `.github/workflows/auto-response.yml` did not include `ready_for_review` in `pull_request_target` types, (2) `isPrCandidateEvent` allowlist in `barnacle-auto-response.mjs` did not include `ready_for_review`, and (3) `applyPullRequestCandidateLabels` was add-only (never removed stale labels).
- Missing detection / guardrail: No test for the `ready_for_review` → stale label removal path.
- Contributing context (if known): N/A

## Real behavior proof

Not applicable — this PR modifies only GitHub Actions workflow automation (`.github/workflows/auto-response.yml`).
No product code, CLI, gateway, plugin, or UI surface is touched.
Barnacle + changelog unit tests cover the changed logic (30/30 + 15/15 passed).

- Scenario the test should lock in: `ready_for_review` action removes stale candidate labels when PR body becomes meaningful
- Why this is the smallest reliable guardrail: Directly exercises `applyPullRequestCandidateLabels` return value + `removeLabels` call path
- Existing test that already covers this (if any): None — this was a new coverage gap
- If no new test is added, why not: N/A

## User-visible / Behavior Changes

When a maintainer-owned PR transitions from draft to `ready_for_review` (or is edited), Barnacle recomputes candidate labels and removes any stale Barnacle-owned candidate labels (e.g. `triage: blank-template`) that no longer match the PR body/files.

## Diagram (if applicable)

```text
Before:
[PR ready_for_review] -> [add missing labels only] -> [stale labels persist]

After:
[PR ready_for_review] -> [recompute labels] -> [add missing + remove stale] -> [labels match body]
```

1. Open a draft PR with a blank issue template body

target.title: fix(commitments): stop hardcoding fastMode in extraction (#78451)
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves
MiniMax Coding Plan users whose token plan includes `MiniMax-M2.7` but not `MiniMax-M2.7-highspeed` could not run commitment extraction because the hidden extraction path hardcoded `fastMode: true`, silently rewriting the selected model to the unsupported highspeed variant.

## Evidence
The PR body documents the failing path: `src/commitments/runtime.ts` passed `fastMode: true` into `runEmbeddedPiAgent`, and `src/agents/pi-embedded-runner/minimax-stream-wrappers.ts` rewrote the model id to `-highspeed`. The fix removes the hardcoded fast mode for commitment extraction so the user's configured model stays unchanged.

---

## Summary

MiniMax Coding Plan operators whose plan owns `MiniMax-M2.7` but not the `-highspeed` variant hit `HTTP 500: your current token plan not support model, MiniMax-M2.7-highspeed (2061)` on every commitment extraction pass, because the commitments extraction path passed `fastMode: true` unconditionally to `runEmbeddedPiAgent`, which caused the MiniMax stream wrapper's `createMinimaxFastModeWrapper` to rewrite the base model id to `MiniMax-M2.7-highspeed`.

## Root Cause

- `src/commitments/runtime.ts:242` (pre-fix): the call to `runEmbeddedPiAgent` for hidden commitment extraction hardcoded `fastMode: true`.
- `src/agents/pi-embedded-runner/minimax-stream-wrappers.ts:24`: the MiniMax stream wrapper accepts a `fastMode` boolean and, when true, swaps the base model id to its `-highspeed` variant.
- Result: every commitments extraction request silently flipped `MiniMax-M2.7` → `MiniMax-M2.7-highspeed`, which Coding Plan operators do not own. MiniMax responds with HTTP 500 / error code 2061. Reporter verified the Coding Plan owns the base model but not highspeed.
- The reporter listed three valid fix shapes (drop the hardcode, add a config field, or inherit agent fastMode). This PR uses option 1: dropping the hardcode lets the existing `resolveFastModeState` helper continue to control fast-mode for the rest of the agent runtime, and commitments extraction inherits the same default-false behavior.

## Changes

- `src/commitments/runtime.ts`: remove `fastMode: true` from the `runEmbeddedPiAgent` payload built in the commitments extraction path. Add a comment explaining the reason so this does not regress.
- `src/commitments/runtime.test.ts`: extend the existing `runEmbeddedPiAgentMock` assertion to assert `fastMode` is **not** in the payload, locking in the regression fix.
- `CHANGELOG.md`: single-line entry under Unreleased / Fixes.

## Real behavior proof

- Behavior addressed: On every commitment extraction pass, MiniMax Coding Plan operators receive `HTTP 500: your current token plan not support model, MiniMax-M2.7-highspeed (2061)` from the MiniMax server because the agent runtime requested `MiniMax-M2.7-highspeed` even though their plan only owns `MiniMax-M2.7`. The reporter (`@advaitpaliwal`) verified `commitments.enabled: true, commitments.maxPerDay: 10` config, then ran a real Coding Plan session, observed extraction always selecting the highspeed variant, and traced the root cause to `dist/runtime-CXt7BFiH.js` line 386 (`fastMode: true` hardcoded). target.title: fix(cli): one-shot agent --local runs never export OTel diagnostics
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Fixes an issue where one-shot `openclaw agent --local` runs would export no OTel telemetry at all when `diagnostics.otel.enabled: true` and the `diagnostics-otel` plugin are configured: zero spans, metrics, or logs reached the OTLP collector, while the same turns dispatched through the Gateway exported fine. Gateway-to-embedded fallback runs (gateway timeout or transport failure) silently dropped telemetry the same way, so exactly the runs that bypass the Gateway were invisible in tracing backends.

## Why This Change Was Made

Diagnostics exporters are plugin services and were only ever started inside the Gateway process (`startPluginServices` at gateway startup/reload); embedded CLI runs emit diagnostic events in the CLI process where nothing subscribes. The CLI now starts the `diagnostics-otel` service around embedded agent runs via a scoped, non-activating plugin load that honors the same plugin-enablement config as the Gateway, and flushes on exit: drain the async diagnostic-event queue, then shut the SDK down (force flush), bounded by a 10s timeout so an unreachable collector cannot hang the CLI. `diagnostics-prometheus` intentionally stays Gateway-only — it is a pull-based scrape server that is useless in a short-lived process and would race the Gateway for its port. No new config surface; configs without OTel enabled short-circuit before any plugin load.

## User Impact

Operators running one-shot `openclaw agent --local` turns (and runs that fall back from the Gateway to the embedded agent) now get the same OTel traces, metrics, and logs as Gateway-executed turns, flushed before the process exits. Setups without OTel export enabled are unaffected.

## Evidence

- Live before/after on macOS against a local Arize Phoenix OTLP collector: before, one-shot `--local` runs produced zero spans while Gateway runs exported fine; after, a one-shot run logs `diagnostics-otel: logs exporter enabled (OTLP/Protobuf)` and `openclaw.harness.run`, `openclaw.run`, and `openclaw.model.call` spans (with `gen_ai.*` attributes) arrive in Phoenix seconds after the process exits.
- New focused tests: `src/plugins/one-shot-diagnostics.test.ts` covers config gating (no plugin load when OTel is off), the scoped non-activating load, exporter allowlist filtering, drain-before-stop ordering, and the flush timeout bound; `src/commands/agent-via-gateway.test.ts` adds cases for start/flush ordering around local runs, flush when the embedded run fails, run survival when exporter startup fails, exporter start on gateway-to-embedded fallback, and no exporter on Gateway dispatch. Both files pass (9 + 73 tests) rebased on current `main`.
- `pnpm build` clean with no `[INEFFECTIVE_DYNAMIC_IMPORT]` warnings; `tsgo` core and test lanes clean; oxfmt/oxlint clean on touched files. Validation ran locally via `scripts/run-vitest.mjs` (remote Testbox was unavailable in this environment).

target.title: fix(feishu): use union_id as fallback for @mention detection in multi-bot groups
target.body:
## Problem

Fixes #40768

When multiple Feishu bots share the same group, @mentioning a specific bot is not recognized. The bot logs `message in group ... did not mention bot` even though it's correctly mentioned.

## Root Cause

Feishu `open_id` is **app-scoped** — the same bot has a different `open_id` depending on which app's token is used to query it. Confirmed by querying the same message with two different bot tokens:

```
# Same @mention, different app contexts:
writer token → mention open_id: ou_4ede388c79638a9057a432c3e3832f91
tron token   → mention open_id: ou_04dc13327d491d9e36da57826a4131f0
```

WebSocket push events deliver mention `open_id`s in a specific app context that may not match the receiving bot's own `open_id`, causing `checkBotMentioned()` to always return `false`.

## Fix

`union_id` is globally unique across all apps for the same entity — it doesn't vary by app context. This PR:

1. Fetches `union_id` alongside `open_id` from `bot/v3/info` at startup
2. Stores it in a new `botUnionIds` map in monitor state
3. Passes it through to `checkBotMentioned()` as a fallback
4. Matches mentions by `union_id` when `open_id` doesn't match

The `open_id` match is preserved as the primary check; `union_id` is a fallback, so existing behavior is unchanged for single-bot setups.

## Files Changed

- `types.ts`: add `botUnionId` to `FeishuProbeResult`
- `probe.ts`: extract `union_id` from `bot/v3/info` response
- `monitor.startup.ts`: propagate `botUnionId` through `FeishuMonitorBotIdentity`
- `monitor.state.ts`: add `botUnionIds` map with proper clear/delete
- `monitor.account.ts`: store/clear `botUnionId`, pass to `handleFeishuMessage`
- `bot.ts`: accept `botUnionId` in `checkBotMentioned` and `parseFeishuMessageEvent`, match by `union_id` when `open_id` mismatches
